title: SDK Grove: Five-Step Onboarding Notebook
body:
Purpose:
This notebook is a low-friction, opinionated five-step onboarding pathway for new SDK adopters and internal engineers trying out Redwood features for the first time. The 'Grove' metaphor: small, repeatable experiments that grow into production patterns. Keep it short, workable, and explicit about failure modes.

Audience:
- IC engineers doing a 1-2 hour sandbox run
- Solutions engineers preparing a 15-minute demo
- New devexp team hires who need a runnable checklist

High-level flow (the five steps)
1) Seed: 0->hello (10m)
  - Goal: make an API call and receive a response.
  - Action: set REDWOOD_API_KEY in a temporary shell, run minimal curl or js snippet below.
  - Smoke command (bash):
    export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' -d '{"model":"rwd-small-1","input":"hello"}'
  - Acceptance: non-empty text response, <2s for local dev env.

2) Seedling: sample app + telemetry (30-45m)
  - Goal: wire the SDK into a tiny app and capture basic telemetry.
  - Steps: clone the sample app repo (link above), add API key to .env, enable SDK telemetry flag (DEVEXP_TELEMETRY=on).
  - Telemetry probes: record latency, token_count, and error_rate for first 50 requests.
  - Quick checks: open trace in Console > requests > recent. Expect a per-request token breakdown.

3) Thicket: prompt-set + quality guard (30-60m)
  - Goal: validate a small prompt suite against the chosen model and assert baseline quality.
  - Use: 8-10 seed prompts (customer type: search assistant, summarizer, classify).
  - Run local eval harness (scripts/eval_local.sh). Record top-3 failure modes.
  - If hallucination rate > 10% -> add system instruction + reranking route.

4) Grove-run: failover + cost knobting (20-40m)
  - Goal: exercise routing and cost controls.
  - Configure: set up a route policy that prefers 'rwd-fast-1' but falls back to 'rwd-compact-1' on 95th pct latency or on quota_exhausted.
  - Simulate: run a small load generator (tools/loadtoy.py --rps 10 --duration 60s) and confirm fallback triggers.
  - Cost knobs: enable caching of prefix for static prompts and test token savings.

5) Orchard: handoff checklist & next steps (10-20m)
  - Goal: leave the experiment in a reproducible, shareable state for later productionization.
  - Deliverables: short PR with env.example, README.md that lists the exact model, route config, and 5 failing prompts plus remediation notes. Link to the Confluence page.

Quicknotes / heuristics (tacit knowledge)
- Keep sample prompt sets small; bigger corpora belong in Optimize.
- Prefer explicit token budget in dev env (DEV_TOKEN_LIMIT=1000) to catch runaway loops.
- For demos, pre-warm the model once to avoid cold-start jitter.
- Use local model stubbing if needing to show offline demos.

Failure-mode catalog (work-in-progress)
- 401/invalid-key: user accidentally installed old creds; suggest rotate and check prefix.
- High-latency spikes: likely inefficent prompt or large context; try shorter instructions, enable async streaming.
- Quality regressions after a model bump: compare sample-suite diffs and pin model version in route.

TODOs (next edits)
- Add minimal Node + Python snippets for step 1 (Aisha to author).
- Small diagram for routing policy (Devon).
- Add CI job example to run the 10-prompt smoke eval on PRs (Priya).

Notes to self:
- This should feel like a 90-minute ritual you can run in a hotel room with a laptop and mobile hotspot. Keep dependencies to node 18 or python 3.10 max.
- Callouts for SEs: include one two-minute fallback demo they can run during an onboarding call.

References and quick links:
- Sample repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdkgrove-sample (prototype)
- Console traces: Console > Requests > [sample-app]
- Eval harness: scripts/eval_local.sh

End of notebook.
